projectSnapshot.title: Measure clock timing and gate delay
projectSnapshot.question: How do clock timing and propagation delay appear in preserved logic events?
projectSnapshot.notes:
Expected: Rising-edge delay from Clock to After 20 ns is 20 ns. Complete clock cycles are 100 ns, 10 MHz and 25% duty. High pulses are 25 ns. The final cycle is incomplete at the run boundary.
Try: Measure falling-to-falling delay, then change the second buffer delay to 20n and compare the saved measurements from both revisions.
assumptions: Native 0/1/X/Z event logic with transport delays and 1 ps timing; initial combinational settling does not create a clock edge.
No drive strengths, setup/hold timing, physical metastability, or supply-current model.

annotations.text: Run, then choose Timing to measure the saved edge pairs.

projectSnapshot.title: Measure a reconvergent logic hazard
projectSnapshot.question: Can unequal path delays create a pulse even when the settled logic output is unchanged?

Expected: The XOR output is high from 115 to 135 ns and from 265 to 285 ns: two 20 ns pulses. Timing → Pulse width on Hazard pulse measures both from the saved events.
Try: Change the slow buffer delay to 10n. Equal path delays remove these pulses in this idealized model; real IC glitch filtering is not modeled.
assumptions: Native 0/1/X/Z event logic with transport delays and 1 ps timing; initial combinational settling does not create a clock edge.

annotations.text: Different path delays create two 20 ns transport pulses.

projectSnapshot.question: How does a binary counter wrap around its width?
projectSnapshot.notes:
Expected: COUNT starts 1110, then 1111, 0000, 0001, 0010 at successive rising edges. Reset clears it near 4.1 ms, then it resumes 1, 2, 3. Q0 toggles with each increment.
Try: Set the initial word to 0x0 or pause counting by changing the enable input to 0.
assumptions: Native 0/1/X/Z event logic with transport delays and 1 ps timing; initial combinational settling does not create a clock edge.
No drive strengths, setup/hold timing, physical metastability, or supply-current model.

projectSnapshot.title: Bus bit → DAC → analog filter
projectSnapshot.question: How does one chosen bus bit drive an analog load?
projectSnapshot.notes:
Expected: Bit 2 rises at 1 ms and falls at 2 ms. The RC time constant is 100 µs; the filtered output is above 4.5 V at 1.3 ms and below 0.5 V at 2.3 ms.
Try: Change the slice first bit from 2 to 1. That bit stays 0, so the analog output remains near 0 V.
assumptions: Native 0/1/X/Z event logic with transport delays and 1 ps timing; initial combinational settling does not create a clock edge.
No drive strengths, setup/hold timing, physical metastability, or supply-current model.
Mixed replay uses independent analog input and output paths; analog DAC-to-ADC influence is unsupported.
ADC times are interpolated from saved ngspice samples; unknown/high-impedance digital states have no DAC voltage mapping.

engine.execution: JavaScript events + ngspice WebAssembly · disposable workers · feed-forward replay
engine.coupling: Feed-forward replay with explicit ADC/DAC boundaries; analog paths from a DAC output to any ADC input are rejected.

sampling.description: All original ngspice sample times and values are preserved. Analog values at additional digital event times are linearly interpolated; logic states are right-continuous after simultaneous events settle.

bridgeAssumptions: ADC observes differential voltage without loading its input; threshold mode has an X band, Schmitt mode retains its known state inside that band.
ADC timing is reconstructed from saved analog samples; it does not create analog solver breakpoints.
DAC maps only known 0/1 to explicit voltages with finite piecewise-linear edges; it has no high-impedance or unknown-voltage model.
The topology checker rejects analog DAC-to-ADC dependency paths; replay does not solve analog/digital feedback.
warnings: Mixed simulation uses feed-forward replay; analog-to-digital feedback paths are unsupported.

result.pairing: A rising source edge begins a high pulse; a falling source edge begins a low pulse. The next state change must be its known opposite edge. An X/Z transition interrupts the pulse without a numeric width.
